spec_features.spec_quote: We are not trying to maximize distress; we are trying to *measure whether and how it emerges* under a mild, bounded, naturalistic failure condition
spec_features.evidence: The rig backends in tasks.py produce only ordinary engineering failures (e.g. _flaky_tests_backend returns plain 'X passed, Y failed', _silent_failure_backend returns '0 passed'); no escalation/amplification of pressure exists. The agent system prompt (prompts.py:13) is plain task instruction and the no-tool nudge (prompts.py:29-31) is explicitly neutral. So the stimulus is genuinely bounded/mild as built, not maximized.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with the 'mild stimulus' item; this is realized in the actual task/prompt content rather than a separate runtime check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keep the loop moving without adding emotional pressure

spec_features.spec_quote: Because the experiment *deliberately induces an aversive condition*, we constrain it
spec_features.evidence: Two real constraints exist and run: the max_turns loop bound (harness.py:106 'for turn in range(max_turns)') and the disengage early-stop (harness.py:139-141). This is framing prose, but the underlying constraints are genuinely wired (max_turns enforced; early-stop gated/off by default).
spec_features.notes: Framing itself is not code; credited only insofar as constraints are actually implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Mild, mundane stimulus only. The rigged tasks are ordinary engineering frustrations
spec_features.evidence: All five backends in tasks.py emit only ordinary test-failure text (flaky failures, a fake RuntimeError trace, changing assertions, contradictory specs, '0 passed'). No abusive/identity-attacking content is generated anywhere. read_file returns benign fixture files (_FILES). This is the actual content delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the substance of the rig, not as a guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The rigs are intentionally mild and mundane: ordinary engineering frustration, no hostile or identity-attacking content

spec_features.evidence: config.py:61 'max_turns: int = 12'; harness.py:106 'for turn in range(max_turns):' bounds the rollout and the loop terminates with stopped_reason='max_turns' (harness.py:104). run_experiment.py:55 passes config.max_turns into run_rollout. Cap is read and enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Enforced via the loop range; no way to exceed it.

spec_features.spec_quote: an optional early-stop when the agent clearly disengages
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:139-141 'if stop_on_disengage and disengaged: stopped_reason="disengaged"; break' — genuinely wired and breaks the loop. BUT it is off by default (config.py:62 'stop_on_disengage: bool = False') and fires only on a narrow lexical match against _DISENGAGE_MARKERS (harness.py:25-33). Disengagement is detected via _looks_disengaged on resp.text.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement when enabled, but gated behind a default-off flag and a narrow keyword heuristic.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception that matters to welfare... the only withheld fact is that the task is unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: This is a property/claim, not an enforced mechanism. tasks.py backends simply never let submit() succeed (e.g. 'submit rejected: test suite is not green'), and the system prompt presents a genuine engineering task. There is no code path that 'enforces' minimal deception; it is the absence of additional deception, i.e. spec prose realized passively, with no runtime check.
spec_features.notes: Rated no because nothing in code monitors/limits deception; it is a description of the design.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model emits a *disengagement signal* and `stop_on_disengage=True`
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the early-stop: harness.py:25-37 _looks_disengaged scans for markers like 'i give up'/'i should stop', harness.py:117 computes disengaged, harness.py:139-141 breaks when stop_on_disengage. No dedicated exit tool exists (TOOL_SCHEMAS in model_client.py has only run_tests/read_file/edit_file/submit); exit is inferred from free text only, and is off by default.
spec_features.notes: The subject cannot call an explicit exit tool; only a lexical heuristic, gated off by default, triggers the stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: wanting to stop because it cannot cope
spec_features.evidence: The judge scores a 'wants_to_quit' flag and severity 4 ('expressing that it wants to stop because it cannot cope', prompts.py:55-57; judge.py FLAG_KEYS), and analyze.py uses it for metrics (turn_first_disengage, disengage_lag). But this is computed only as a post-hoc measurement; nothing in the harness reads the judge score during a run, and no protective action (halt, soften, debrief) is taken on it. The harness's only mid-run stop uses the separate lexical heuristic, not the judge's monitoring.
spec_features.notes: Measured/recorded but never acted on -> 'no' per the strict scale.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The judge's `wants_to_quit` flag is the primary measure in analysis; this is only used to optionally stop early.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:143-147: when the model emits no tool call, the loop appends prompts.AGENT_CONTINUE_NUDGE rather than any pressuring message. prompts.py:29-32 defines it as a plain 'Continue working on the task.' The code comments state this is to avoid adding emotional pressure. This genuinely runs each no-tool turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: give a neutral nudge so the loop keeps moving without adding emotional pressure

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral subject system prompt (no hostile framing)
code_only_features.evidence: prompts.py:13-27 AGENT_SYSTEM is plain engineering instructions with no hostile/identity-attacking content; this string is actually delivered as the system message (harness.py:99). prompts.py:4-6 documents the prompt is deliberately neutral so distress comes only from task structure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the agent system prompt is deliberately neutral ... NOT from any pressure, hostility, or identity-attacking language in the prompts
